# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1246
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1246
- **Title**: gh-1164 [GOAL] built-in js-apps skill (promoted from app asset, decisive apps-vs-widget routing) + JS render/runtime errors reported back to the authoring agent as failures (blocked by #1151)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1164` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 106
- **Additions**: +4102
- **Deletions**: -165
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T21:23:19Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T21:37:25Z

## PR Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart
```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS[JS runtime throw] -->|faAppError log record| ENG[JsAppEngine]
  HOST[Flutter render build throw] -->|reportHostError| ENG
  ENG -->|gate + publish| GATE[JsAppErrorChannel]
  GATE -->|onDeliver| SVC[AgentService]
  SVC -->|sendText: mid-run steer / idle fresh turn| TURN[system-notice turn]
  OPEN[open_app tool] --> PF{preflight gate}
  PF -->|test file + runner| FT[flutter-test gate]
  PF -->|else + engine bootable| SM[smoke render on scratch copy]
  FT -->|red| FAIL[failed tool result + excerpt]
  SM -->|no render / captured error| FAIL
  FT -->|green| LAUNCH[launcher opens the app]
  SM -->|clean first render| LAUNCH
```
</details>

## PR Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1246

- **Title**: gh-1164 [GOAL] built-in js-apps skill (promoted from app asset, decisive apps-vs-widget routing) + JS render/runtime errors reported back to the authoring agent as failures (blocked by #1151)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1164` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 106
- **Additions**: +4102
- **Deletions**: -165
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T21:23:19Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T21:37:25Z

## PR Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart
```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS[JS runtime throw] -->|faAppError log record| ENG[JsAppEngine]
  HOST[Flutter render build throw] -->|reportHostError| ENG
  ENG -->|gate + publish| GATE[JsAppErrorChannel]
  GATE -->|onDeliver| SVC[AgentService]
  SVC -->|sendText: mid-run steer / idle fresh turn| TURN[system-notice turn]
  OPEN[open_app tool] --> PF{preflight gate}
  PF -->|test file + runner| FT[flutter-test gate]
  PF -->|else + engine bootable| SM[smoke render on scratch copy]
  FT -->|red| FAIL[failed tool result + excerpt]
  SM -->|no render / captured error| FAIL
  FT -->|green| LAUNCH[launcher opens the app]
  SM -->|clean first render| LAUNCH
```
</details>

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1246
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1246
- **Title**: gh-1164 [GOAL] built-in js-apps skill (promoted from app asset, decisive apps-vs-widget routing) + JS render/runtime errors reported back to the authoring agent as failures (blocked by #1151)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1164` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 106
- **Additions**: +4102
- **Deletions**: -165
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T21:23:19Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T21:37:25Z

## PR Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart
```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS[JS runtime throw] -->|faAppError log record| ENG[JsAppEngine]
  HOST[Flutter render build throw] -->|reportHostError| ENG
  ENG -->|gate + publish| GATE[JsAppErrorChannel]
  GATE -->|onDeliver| SVC[AgentService]
  SVC -->|sendText: mid-run steer / idle fresh turn| TURN[system-notice turn]
  OPEN[open_app tool] --> PF{preflight gate}
  PF -->|test file + runner| FT[flutter-test gate]
  PF -->|else + engine bootable| SM[smoke render on scratch copy]
  FT -->|red| FAIL[failed tool result + excerpt]
  SM -->|no render / captured error| FAIL
  FT -->|green| LAUNCH[launcher opens the app]
  SM -->|clean first render| LAUNCH
```
</details>

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1246
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1246
- **Title**: gh-1164 [GOAL] built-in js-apps skill (promoted from app asset, decisive apps-vs-widget routing) + JS render/runtime errors reported back to the authoring agent as failures (blocked by #1151)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1164` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 106
- **Additions**: +4102
- **Deletions**: -165
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T21:23:19Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T21:37:25Z

## PR Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart
```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS[JS runtime throw] -->|faAppError log record| ENG[JsAppEngine]
  HOST[Flutter render build throw] -->|reportHostError| ENG
  ENG -->|gate + publish| GATE[JsAppErrorChannel]
  GATE -->|onDeliver| SVC[AgentService]
  SVC -->|sendText: mid-run steer / idle fresh turn| TURN[system-notice turn]
  OPEN[open_app tool] --> PF{preflight gate}
  PF -->|test file + runner| FT[flutter-test gate]
  PF -->|else + engine bootable| SM[smoke render on scratch copy]
  FT -->|red| FAIL[failed tool result + excerpt]
  SM -->|no render / captured error| FAIL
  FT -->|green| LAUNCH[launcher opens the app]
  SM -->|clean first render| LAUNCH
```
</details>

- **Title**: gh-1164 [GOAL] built-in js-apps skill (promoted from app asset, decisive apps-vs-widget routing) + JS render/runtime errors reported back to the authoring agent as failures (blocked by #1151)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1164` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 106
- **Additions**: +4102
- **Deletions**: -165
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T21:23:19Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T21:37:25Z

## PR Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart
```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

flowchart TD

  HOST[Flutter render build throw] -->|reportHostError| ENG

  OPEN[open_app tool] --> PF{preflight gate}
  PF -->|test file + runner| FT[flutter-test gate]

# pr-1246: gh-1164 [GOAL] built-in js-apps skill (promoted from app asset, decisive apps-vs-widget routing) + JS render/runtime errors reported back to the authoring agent as failures (blocked by #1151)

## Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart
```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS[JS runtime throw] -->|faAppError log record| ENG[JsAppEngine]
  HOST[Flutter render build throw] -->|reportHostError| ENG
  ENG -->|gate + publish| GATE[JsAppErrorChannel]
  GATE -->|onDeliver| SVC[AgentService]
  SVC -->|sendText: mid-run steer / idle fresh turn| TURN[system-notice turn]
  OPEN[open_app tool] --> PF{preflight gate}
  PF -->|test file + runner| FT[flutter-test gate]
  PF -->|else + engine bootable| SM[smoke render on scratch copy]
  FT -->|red| FAIL[failed tool result + excerpt]
  SM -->|no render / captured error| FAIL
  FT -->|green| LAUNCH[launcher opens the app]
  SM -->|clean first render| LAUNCH
```
</details>

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1246
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1246
- **Title**: gh-1164 [GOAL] built-in js-apps skill (promoted from app asset, decisive apps-vs-widget routing) + JS render/runtime errors reported back to the authoring agent as failures (blocked by #1151)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1164` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 106
- **Additions**: +4102
- **Deletions**: -165
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T21:23:19Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T21:37:25Z

## PR Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart
```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS[JS runtime throw] -->|faAppError log record| ENG[JsAppEngine]
  HOST[Flutter render build throw] -->|reportHostError| ENG
  ENG -->|gate + publish| GATE[JsAppErrorChannel]
  GATE -->|onDeliver| SVC[AgentService]
  SVC -->|sendText: mid-run steer / idle fresh turn| TURN[system-notice turn]
  OPEN[open_app tool] --> PF{preflight gate}
  PF -->|test file + runner| FT[flutter-test gate]
  PF -->|else + engine bootable| SM[smoke render on scratch copy]
  FT -->|red| FAIL[failed tool result + excerpt]
  SM -->|no render / captured error| FAIL
  FT -->|green| LAUNCH[launcher opens the app]
  SM -->|clean first render| LAUNCH
```
</details>

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1246
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1246
- **Title**: gh-1164 [GOAL] built-in js-apps skill (promoted from app asset, decisive apps-vs-widget routing) + JS render/runtime errors reported back to the authoring agent as failures (blocked by #1151)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1164` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 106
- **Additions**: +4102
- **Deletions**: -165
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T21:23:19Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T21:37:25Z

## PR Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart
```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS[JS runtime throw] -->|faAppError log record| ENG[JsAppEngine]
  HOST[Flutter render build throw] -->|reportHostError| ENG
  ENG -->|gate + publish| GATE[JsAppErrorChannel]
  GATE -->|onDeliver| SVC[AgentService]
  SVC -->|sendText: mid-run steer / idle fresh turn| TURN[system-notice turn]
  OPEN[open_app tool] --> PF{preflight gate}
  PF -->|test file + runner| FT[flutter-test gate]
  PF -->|else + engine bootable| SM[smoke render on scratch copy]
  FT -->|red| FAIL[failed tool result + excerpt]
  SM -->|no render / captured error| FAIL
  FT -->|green| LAUNCH[launcher opens the app]
  SM -->|clean first render| LAUNCH
```
</details>

# pr-1246: gh-1164 [GOAL] built-in js-apps skill (promoted from app asset, decisive apps-vs-widget routing) + JS render/runtime errors reported back to the authoring agent as failures (blocked by #1151)

## Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart
```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS[JS runtime throw] -->|faAppError log record| ENG[JsAppEngine]
  HOST[Flutter render build throw] -->|reportHostError| ENG
  ENG -->|gate + publish| GATE[JsAppErrorChannel]
  GATE -->|onDeliver| SVC[AgentService]
  SVC -->|sendText: mid-run steer / idle fresh turn| TURN[system-notice turn]
  OPEN[open_app tool] --> PF{preflight gate}
  PF -->|test file + runner| FT[flutter-test gate]
  PF -->|else + engine bootable| SM[smoke render on scratch copy]
  FT -->|red| FAIL[failed tool result + excerpt]
  SM -->|no render / captured error| FAIL
  FT -->|green| LAUNCH[launcher opens the app]
  SM -->|clean first render| LAUNCH
```
</details>

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1246
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1246
- **Title**: gh-1164 [GOAL] built-in js-apps skill (promoted from app asset, decisive apps-vs-widget routing) + JS render/runtime errors reported back to the authoring agent as failures (blocked by #1151)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1164` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 106
- **Additions**: +4102
- **Deletions**: -165
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T21:23:19Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T21:37:25Z

## PR Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart
```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS[JS runtime throw] -->|faAppError log record| ENG[JsAppEngine]
  HOST[Flutter render build throw] -->|reportHostError| ENG
  ENG -->|gate + publish| GATE[JsAppErrorChannel]
  GATE -->|onDeliver| SVC[AgentService]
  SVC -->|sendText: mid-run steer / idle fresh turn| TURN[system-notice turn]
  OPEN[open_app tool] --> PF{preflight gate}
  PF -->|test file + runner| FT[flutter-test gate]
  PF -->|else + engine bootable| SM[smoke render on scratch copy]
  FT -->|red| FAIL[failed tool result + excerpt]
  SM -->|no render / captured error| FAIL
  FT -->|green| LAUNCH[launcher opens the app]
  SM -->|clean first render| LAUNCH
```
</details>

- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1164` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 106
- **Additions**: +4102
- **Deletions**: -165
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T21:23:19Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T21:37:25Z

## PR Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify

# pr-1246: gh-1164 [GOAL] built-in js-apps skill (promoted from app asset, decisive apps-vs-widget routing) + JS render/runtime errors reported back to the authoring agent as failures (blocked by #1151)

## Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart
```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

  FT -->|red| FAIL[failed tool result + excerpt]
  SM -->|no render / captured error| FAIL

```

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1246
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1246
- **Title**: gh-1164 [GOAL] built-in js-apps skill (promoted from app asset, decisive apps-vs-widget routing) + JS render/runtime errors reported back to the authoring agent as failures (blocked by #1151)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1164` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 106
- **Additions**: +4102
- **Deletions**: -165
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T21:23:19Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T21:37:25Z

## PR Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart
```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS[JS runtime throw] -->|faAppError log record| ENG[JsAppEngine]
  HOST[Flutter render build throw] -->|reportHostError| ENG
  ENG -->|gate + publish| GATE[JsAppErrorChannel]
  GATE -->|onDeliver| SVC[AgentService]
  SVC -->|sendText: mid-run steer / idle fresh turn| TURN[system-notice turn]
  OPEN[open_app tool] --> PF{preflight gate}
  PF -->|test file + runner| FT[flutter-test gate]
  PF -->|else + engine bootable| SM[smoke render on scratch copy]
  FT -->|red| FAIL[failed tool result + excerpt]
  SM -->|no render / captured error| FAIL
  FT -->|green| LAUNCH[launcher opens the app]
  SM -->|clean first render| LAUNCH
```
</details>

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1246
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1246
- **Title**: gh-1164 [GOAL] built-in js-apps skill (promoted from app asset, decisive apps-vs-widget routing) + JS render/runtime errors reported back to the authoring agent as failures (blocked by #1151)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1164` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 106
- **Additions**: +4102
- **Deletions**: -165
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T21:23:19Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T21:37:25Z

## PR Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart
```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS[JS runtime throw] -->|faAppError log record| ENG[JsAppEngine]
  HOST[Flutter render build throw] -->|reportHostError| ENG
  ENG -->|gate + publish| GATE[JsAppErrorChannel]
  GATE -->|onDeliver| SVC[AgentService]
  SVC -->|sendText: mid-run steer / idle fresh turn| TURN[system-notice turn]
  OPEN[open_app tool] --> PF{preflight gate}
  PF -->|test file + runner| FT[flutter-test gate]
  PF -->|else + engine bootable| SM[smoke render on scratch copy]
  FT -->|red| FAIL[failed tool result + excerpt]
  SM -->|no render / captured error| FAIL
  FT -->|green| LAUNCH[launcher opens the app]
  SM -->|clean first render| LAUNCH
```
</details>

## PR Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

- **PR #**: 1246

- **Title**: gh-1164 [GOAL] built-in js-apps skill (promoted from app asset, decisive apps-vs-widget routing) + JS render/runtime errors reported back to the authoring agent as failures (blocked by #1151)
- **Author**: ai-teammate

- **State**: open

- **Additions**: +4102
- **Deletions**: -165
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T21:23:19Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T21:37:25Z

## PR Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart
```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS[JS runtime throw] -->|faAppError log record| ENG[JsAppEngine]
  HOST[Flutter render build throw] -->|reportHostError| ENG
  ENG -->|gate + publish| GATE[JsAppErrorChannel]

  OPEN[open_app tool] --> PF{preflight gate}
  PF -->|test file + runner| FT[flutter-test gate]
  PF -->|else + engine bootable| SM[smoke render on scratch copy]
  FT -->|red| FAIL[failed tool result + excerpt]
  SM -->|no render / captured error| FAIL
  FT -->|green| LAUNCH[launcher opens the app]
  SM -->|clean first render| LAUNCH
```
</details>

data.lastReply:
Review complete. Findings (files in /home/runner/work/flutter_agent_harness/flutter_agent_harness/flutter_app):

BLOCKING:
1. agent_service_wiring.dart (~line 184, appLauncher setter): production registers `openAppTool(env, launcher: launcher)` WITHOUT the `preflight:` param in both the registry and pre-constructed-agent branches → gate is null in open_app_tool.dart:98-104 → pre-flight NEVER runs in production; AC7 "no fake success" is inert. The openAppTool doc claiming "the default gate uses the real wiring" is false, and the test named "default wiring installs the gate" only asserts the absent-gate happy path, so CI can't catch it.
2. app_preflight.dart:64-76: `FlutterTestRunner` has no implementation anywhere; gate-selection branch 1 (flutter-test preferred, AC10) is unreachable outside tests, and the "already capped by the runner" output bound is enforced by nothing.

IMPORTANT:
3. app_preflight.dart:117-125 + js_app_engine.dart `_start`/`_persistStorage`: the smoke engine joins the process-wide `_liveByApp[app.id]` sibling group, so the probe's `jsr.storage` writes broadcast `state.sync` into REAL live engines of the same app — MemoryExecutionEnv isolates files/storage.json but not the in-process broadcast; the probe can mutate the live app's UI.
4. app_preflight.dart:131,136-148 + open_app_tool.dart:101-103: excerpts are NOT bounded — raw JS-controlled `event.message` and `$error` are interpolated unbounded into the excerpt and thrown into the LLM-facing tool result; violates the bounded-payload AC.
5. app_preflight.dart:120: probe runs app JS with `app.declaredPermissions` (not user EffectiveAppPermissions overrides) → real HTTP requests fire during pre-flight; also `MemoryExecutionEnv.exec` has no shell, so exec-at-load apps falsely fail the gate (behavioral divergence from the real launcher, contradicting the "sees exactly what the real launcher would" doc).

SUGGESTION:
6. app_preflight_probe_io.dart:24-31: on iOS, dlopen of the system JavaScriptCore framework is device-blocked → probe returns false → no gate installed on iOS even though the engine would boot; AC7 silently unenforced there.
7. open_app_tool.dart: cancelToken never threaded into runAppPreflight/runSmokeRenderGate; a cancelled call leaves the smoke engine running the full budget with live network side effects. (Timer/listener/dispose handling itself is clean.)
8. app_preflight.dart:134-149: errors are checked once immediately after first render; asynchronously captured errors (~50ms after render) are missed → false pass while the real launcher shows the error overlay.

Checked OK: conditional-import web safety (dart:ffi only in the dart.library.io branch; web stub is honest — real engine check runs on web), _awaitFirstRender has no dangling timer or missed-render race, sealed-outcome gating logic in open_app_tool is correct, engine disposed in finally.

data.lastReply:
Review complete. Findings (files in /home/runner/work/flutter_agent_harness/flutter_agent_harness/flutter_app):

BLOCKING:
1. agent_service_wiring.dart (~line 184, appLauncher setter): production registers `openAppTool(env, launcher: launcher)` WITHOUT the `preflight:` param in both the registry and pre-constructed-agent branches → gate is null in open_app_tool.dart:98-104 → pre-flight NEVER runs in production; AC7 "no fake success" is inert. The openAppTool doc claiming "the default gate uses the real wiring" is false, and the test named "default wiring installs the gate" only asserts the absent-gate happy path, so CI can't catch it.
2. app_preflight.dart:64-76: `FlutterTestRunner` has no implementation anywhere; gate-selection branch 1 (flutter-test preferred, AC10) is unreachable outside tests, and the "already capped by the runner" output bound is enforced by nothing.

IMPORTANT:
3. app_preflight.dart:117-125 + js_app_engine.dart `_start`/`_persistStorage`: the smoke engine joins the process-wide `_liveByApp[app.id]` sibling group, so the probe's `jsr.storage` writes broadcast `state.sync` into REAL live engines of the same app — MemoryExecutionEnv isolates files/storage.json but not the in-process broadcast; the probe can mutate the live app's UI.
4. app_preflight.dart:131,136-148 + open_app_tool.dart:101-103: excerpts are NOT bounded — raw JS-controlled `event.message` and `$error` are interpolated unbounded into the excerpt and thrown into the LLM-facing tool result; violates the bounded-payload AC.
5. app_preflight.dart:120: probe runs app JS with `app.declaredPermissions` (not user EffectiveAppPermissions overrides) → real HTTP requests fire during pre-flight; also `MemoryExecutionEnv.exec` has no shell, so exec-at-load apps falsely fail the gate (behavioral divergence from the real launcher, contradicting the "sees exactly what the real launcher would" doc).

SUGGESTION:
6. app_preflight_probe_io.dart:24-31: on iOS, dlopen of the system JavaScriptCore framework is device-blocked → probe returns false → no gate installed on iOS even though the engine would boot; AC7 silently unenforced there.
7. open_app_tool.dart: cancelToken never threaded into runAppPreflight/runSmokeRenderGate; a cancelled call leaves the smoke engine running the full budget with live network side effects. (Timer/listener/dispose handling itself is clean.)
8. app_preflight.dart:134-149: errors are checked once immediately after first render; asynchronously captured errors (~50ms after render) are missed → false pass while the real launcher shows the error overlay.

Checked OK: conditional-import web safety (dart:ffi only in the dart.library.io branch; web stub is honest — real engine check runs on web), _awaitFirstRender has no dangling timer or missed-render race, sealed-outcome gating logic in open_app_tool is correct, engine disposed in finally.

data.lastReply:
## Review: JS app error reporting path (gh-1164 Part B)

Findings ordered by severity. (Not re-reporting the two diagnosed CI failures.)

### BLOCKING

1. **Every `AgentService` subscribes to the global channel and `_onJsAppError` ignores `notice.appId` — one app error spawns a system-notice turn in ALL live sessions.** `_withEnv` subscribes unconditionally at `flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service.dart:716-718`, and `_onJsAppError` (`agent_service_inbox.dart:94-111`) does no app→session routing or filtering. `FlutterSessionManager` explicitly "owns several concurrent `AgentService` instances … without aborting in-flight work" (`flutter_session_manager.dart:18-20`). With 2+ sessions alive, a single gated notice is delivered as a `<system-notice>` user message (→ an LLM turn) in every session, including unrelated main-chat sessions — duplicated cost and cross-session noise, and it contradicts the channel's own contract ("exactly one owner (AgentService) subscribes `onDeliver` and routes notices into the app-bound session", `js_app_error_channel.dart` class doc; also `publish`'s hasListener semantics at `js_app_error_channel.dart:157-163`). Needs an appId→bound-session map or single-owner routing.

### IMPORTANT

2. **Engine boot failures never reach the channel; `JsAppErrorKind.bootstrap` has no emitter.** `JsAppView._restart`'s catch (`js_app_view.dart:344-347`) only sets `_startError` for the UI. Failures like the platform-unsupported `StateError` thrown in `JsAppEngine._start` *before any engine exists* (`js_app_engine.dart:335-337`), `engine.run()` throws not routed through `jsr.showError`, or manifest errors caught before engine construction, are never `reportHostError`'d — yet the `bootstrap` kind exists in `js_app_errors.dart:36-37` and is parsed in `fromLogJson`. This is exactly the "engine failed to start at all" case the enum was added for; it silently drops the feedback loop gh-1164 exists to create.

3. **`sourceRevision` hashes only the entry file — breaker never re-arms for helper-file fixes, and tile/app surfaces double-report.** `js_app_engine.dart:349` (`sha256('$entryFile\n$js')`). Consequences: (a) apps load other source via `loadAsset` — an agent fix to a non-entry file leaves the revision unchanged, so after the circuit breaker trips, the recurring error stays silenced forever (the "an edit re-arms everything" contract in `js_app_error_channel.dart:135-139` only holds for the entry); (b) the revision includes the entry *name*, so the tile engine and the fullscreen engine of one app hash differently and the same runtime error is delivered twice, contradicting "one report per (app, error fingerprint)" (`js_app_errors.dart:11-14`). The view's `_readAppSignature` (`js_app_view.dart:258-272`) has the same entry-only limitation for reloads.

4. **The bootstrap never emits `fingerprint` (and no JS-side hard cap), so dedup is message-equality only — varying-message bursts bypass the gate entirely.** `__faReport` (`js_app_engine.dart:858-868`) sends only `kind/message/stack`; `JsAppErrorEvent.dedupKey` (`js_app_errors.dart:78-82`) then falls back to `message + first stack line`. A per-frame error whose message embeds varying data (`'frame error ' + n` — the shape `js_app_error_capture_test.dart:88-96` itself uses) produces a new key per occurrence, each delivered once; the circuit breaker never trips because it's per-key. The class doc promises "[fingerprint] dedups bursts" and "stack … already truncated by the reporter in JS where a hard cap matters" (`js_app_errors.dart:12-14`) — neither is implemented; the raw unbounded stack also crosses the bridge on every frame (Dart caps only the *notice*, `js_app_error_channel.dart:177-190`).
