data.lastReply:
## Review: JS app error reporting path (gh-1164 Part B)

Findings ordered by severity. (Not re-reporting the two diagnosed CI failures.)

### BLOCKING

1. **Every `AgentService` subscribes to the global channel and `_onJsAppError` ignores `notice.appId` — one app error spawns a system-notice turn in ALL live sessions.** `_withEnv` subscribes unconditionally at `flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service.dart:716-718`, and `_onJsAppError` (`agent_service_inbox.dart:94-111`) does no app→session routing or filtering. `FlutterSessionManager` explicitly "owns several concurrent `AgentService` instances … without aborting in-flight work" (`flutter_session_manager.dart:18-20`). With 2+ sessions alive, a single gated notice is delivered as a `<system-notice>` user message (→ an LLM turn) in every session, including unrelated main-chat sessions — duplicated cost and cross-session noise, and it contradicts the channel's own contract ("exactly one owner (AgentService) subscribes `onDeliver` and routes notices into the app-bound session", `js_app_error_channel.dart` class doc; also `publish`'s hasListener semantics at `js_app_error_channel.dart:157-163`). Needs an appId→bound-session map or single-owner routing.

### IMPORTANT

2. **Engine boot failures never reach the channel; `JsAppErrorKind.bootstrap` has no emitter.** `JsAppView._restart`'s catch (`js_app_view.dart:344-347`) only sets `_startError` for the UI. Failures like the platform-unsupported `StateError` thrown in `JsAppEngine._start` *before any engine exists* (`js_app_engine.dart:335-337`), `engine.run()` throws not routed through `jsr.showError`, or manifest errors caught before engine construction, are never `reportHostError`'d — yet the `bootstrap` kind exists in `js_app_errors.dart:36-37` and is parsed in `fromLogJson`. This is exactly the "engine failed to start at all" case the enum was added for; it silently drops the feedback loop gh-1164 exists to create.

3. **`sourceRevision` hashes only the entry file — breaker never re-arms for helper-file fixes, and tile/app surfaces double-report.** `js_app_engine.dart:349` (`sha256('$entryFile\n$js')`). Consequences: (a) apps load other source via `loadAsset` — an agent fix to a non-entry file leaves the revision unchanged, so after the circuit breaker trips, the recurring error stays silenced forever (the "an edit re-arms everything" contract in `js_app_error_channel.dart:135-139` only holds for the entry); (b) the revision includes the entry *name*, so the tile engine and the fullscreen engine of one app hash differently and the same runtime error is delivered twice, contradicting "one report per (app, error fingerprint)" (`js_app_errors.dart:11-14`). The view's `_readAppSignature` (`js_app_view.dart:258-272`) has the same entry-only limitation for reloads.

4. **The bootstrap never emits `fingerprint` (and no JS-side hard cap), so dedup is message-equality only — varying-message bursts bypass the gate entirely.** `__faReport` (`js_app_engine.dart:858-868`) sends only `kind/message/stack`; `JsAppErrorEvent.dedupKey` (`js_app_errors.dart:78-82`) then falls back to `message + first stack line`. A per-frame error whose message embeds varying data (`'frame error ' + n` — the shape `js_app_error_capture_test.dart:88-96` itself uses) produces a new key per occurrence, each delivered once; the circuit breaker never trips because it's per-key. The class doc promises "[fingerprint] dedups bursts" and "stack … already truncated by the reporter in JS where a hard cap matters" (`js_app_errors.dart:12-14`) — neither is implemented; the raw unbounded stack also crosses the bridge on every frame (Dart caps only the *notice*, `js_app_error_channel.dart:177-190`).

5. **`reportHostError` misses the render errors it was built for.** `js_app_view.dart:816-826` wraps only `renderer.build(tree, context)` — JSON→Widget *conversion*. Flutter "red screen" errors are thrown later, during element inflation/layout of the returned tree, outside this try/catch, so they're never reported to the agent. Either hook `FlutterError.onError`/an `ErrorBoundary`, or scope the comment/claim to conversion errors only.

### SUGGESTION

6. **Misleading boilerplate on every notice** — `agent_service_inbox.dart:103-107`: "The app source changed since a previous identical report may have been silenced" is appended even to the *first* delivery of a key, asserting something unverified. Reword or gate on `notice` repeat state.

7. **Locale interpolation into the bootstrap strips only `'`** — `js_app_engine.dart:742-746` (`faBootstrapJsFor`). Not injectable (the breakout char is removed) but a locale containing a newline/U+2028 yields a JS syntax error killing the *entire* host bootstrap (all `jsr.fa.*` bridges + error capture). Use `jsonEncode(locale)`. (Verified: app source is executed via `engine.run` and never string-inlined, so quotes/newlines in app code or file paths cannot break the bootstrap — no injection there.)

8. **Error-capture IIFE assigns globals with no per-leg guard** — `js_app_engine.dart:878-894`: `setTimeout`/`setInterval`/`requestAnimationFrame` reassignment and `window.onerror =`/`onunhandledrejection =` run unguarded. One throwing assignment (read-only global in some engine configs) aborts the remaining legs (including the `onerror` leg) and can escape the bootstrap eval; assigning `window.onerror` also clobbers any pre-existing handler — `addEventListener('error'/'unhandledrejection')` composes instead.

9. **Marker spoofing** — `parseJsAppErrorLogLine` (`js_app_error_channel.dart:27-40`) accepts any console line containing `faAppError:{json}`: app code can forge error notices into the agent session (dedup-capped but unauthenticated). Low impact (apps already have `emit`/LLM channels), but worth documenting or namespacing.

10. **Smoke-gate error collector unbounded** — `app_preflight.dart:~113`: `errors.add(...)` for the full 10 s budget with only `errors.first` ever used; a throw-per-frame app accumulates thousands of entries. Cap the list.

### Checked and OK
- Revision is captured at event time correctly (hash of the booting entry, set before `engine.run` at `js_app_engine.dart:349`, read at report time in `_forwardError:445-467`).
- Circuit breaker semantics are intentional: first occurrence delivers, repeats 2–5 return `deliver:false`, then `null` — still a raw log line, not fully silent (`js_app_error_channel.dart:135-153`).
- Payload bounding is correct (message 500, 5 frames/800 chars stack, truncation marked; test asserts < 2000 chars).
- No listener leaks: `AgentService.dispose` cancels `_jsAppErrorSub` (`agent_service.dart` dispose); preflight's `_awaitFirstRender` removes its `tree` listener on both paths (`app_preflight.dart:204-224`); engines push into the channel without subscribing.
- Reentrancy is safe: the broadcast controller is async-by-default, so `_onJsAppError`→`sendText` runs in a later microtask, never inside the engine-log callback or a build; mid-run delivery correctly steers, idle delivery starts a fresh turn.

## Review: JS app error reporting path (gh-1164 Part B)

Findings ordered by severity. (Not re-reporting the two diagnosed CI failures.)

### BLOCKING

1. **Every `AgentService` subscribes to the global channel and `_onJsAppError` ignores `notice.appId` — one app error spawns a system-notice turn in ALL live sessions.** `_withEnv` subscribes unconditionally at `flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service.dart:716-718`, and `_onJsAppError` (`agent_service_inbox.dart:94-111`) does no app→session routing or filtering. `FlutterSessionManager` explicitly "owns several concurrent `AgentService` instances … without aborting in-flight work" (`flutter_session_manager.dart:18-20`). With 2+ sessions alive, a single gated notice is delivered as a `<system-notice>` user message (→ an LLM turn) in every session, including unrelated main-chat sessions — duplicated cost and cross-session noise, and it contradicts the channel's own contract ("exactly one owner (AgentService) subscribes `onDeliver` and routes notices into the app-bound session", `js_app_error_channel.dart` class doc; also `publish`'s hasListener semantics at `js_app_error_channel.dart:157-163`). Needs an appId→bound-session map or single-owner routing.

### IMPORTANT

2. **Engine boot failures never reach the channel; `JsAppErrorKind.bootstrap` has no emitter.** `JsAppView._restart`'s catch (`js_app_view.dart:344-347`) only sets `_startError` for the UI. This is exactly the "engine failed to start at all" case the enum was added for; it silently drops the feedback loop gh-1164 exists to create.

3. **`sourceRevision` hashes only the entry file — breaker never re-arms for helper-file fixes, and tile/app surfaces double-report.** `js_app_engine.dart:349` (`sha256('$entryFile\n$js')`). Consequences: (a) apps load other source via `loadAsset` — an agent fix to a non-entry file leaves the revision unchanged, so after the circuit breaker trips, the recurring error stays silenced forever (the "an edit re-arms everything" contract in `js_app_error_channel.dart:135-139` only holds for the entry); (b) the revision includes the entry *name*, so the tile engine and the fullscreen engine of one app hash differently and the same runtime error is delivered twice, contradicting "one report per (app, error fingerprint)" (`js_app_errors.dart:11-14`). The view's `_readAppSignature` (`js_app_view.dart:258-272`) has the same entry-only limitation for reloads.

4. **The bootstrap never emits `fingerprint` (and no JS-side hard cap), so dedup is message-equality only — varying-message bursts bypass the gate entirely.** `__faReport` (`js_app_engine.dart:858-868`) sends only `kind/message/stack`; `JsAppErrorEvent.dedupKey` (`js_app_errors.dart:78-82`) then falls back to `message + first stack line`. A per-frame error whose message embeds varying data (`'frame error ' + n` — the shape `js_app_error_capture_test.dart:88-96` itself uses) produces a new key per occurrence, each delivered once; the circuit breaker never trips because it's per-key. The class doc promises "[fingerprint] dedups bursts" and "stack … already truncated by the reporter in JS where a hard cap matters" (`js_app_errors.dart:12-14`) — neither is implemented; the raw unbounded stack also crosses the bridge on every frame (Dart caps only the *notice*, `js_app_error_channel.dart:177-190`).

5. **`reportHostError` misses the render errors it was built for.** `js_app_view.dart:816-826` wraps only `renderer.build(tree, context)` — JSON→Widget *conversion*. Flutter "red screen" errors are thrown later, during element inflation/layout of the returned tree, outside this try/catch, so they're never reported to the agent. Either hook `FlutterError.onError`/an `ErrorBoundary`, or scope the comment/claim to conversion errors only.

### SUGGESTION

6. **Misleading boilerplate on every notice** — `agent_service_inbox.dart:103-107`: "The app source changed since a previous identical report may have been silenced" is appended even to the *first* delivery of a key, asserting something unverified. Reword or gate on `notice` repeat state.

7. **Locale interpolation into the bootstrap strips only `'`** — `js_app_engine.dart:742-746` (`faBootstrapJsFor`). Not injectable (the breakout char is removed) but a locale containing a newline/U+2028 yields a JS syntax error killing the *entire* host bootstrap (all `jsr.fa.*` bridges + error capture). Use `jsonEncode(locale)`. (Verified: app source is executed via `engine.run` and never string-inlined, so quotes/newlines in app code or file paths cannot break the bootstrap — no injection there.)

8. **Error-capture IIFE assigns globals with no per-leg guard** — `js_app_engine.dart:878-894`: `setTimeout`/`setInterval`/`requestAnimationFrame` reassignment and `window.onerror =`/`onunhandledrejection =` run unguarded. 10. **Smoke-gate error collector unbounded** — `app_preflight.dart:~113`: `errors.add(...)` for the full 10 s budget with only `errors.first` ever used; a throw-per-frame app accumulates thousands of entries. Cap the list.

### Checked and OK
- Revision is captured at event time correctly (hash of the booting entry, set before `engine.run` at `js_app_engine.dart:349`, read at report time in `_forwardError:445-467`).
- Circuit breaker semantics are intentional: first occurrence delivers, repeats 2–5 return `deliver:false`, then `null` — still a raw log line, not fully silent (`js_app_error_channel.dart:135-153`).

- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1164` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 106
- **Additions**: +4102
- **Deletions**: -165
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T21:23:19Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T21:37:25Z

## PR Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart
```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD

  HOST[Flutter render build throw] -->|reportHostError| ENG
  ENG -->|gate + publish| GATE[JsAppErrorChannel]
  GATE -->|onDeliver| SVC[AgentService]

  OPEN[open_app tool] --> PF{preflight gate}
  PF -->|test file + runner| FT[flutter-test gate]
  PF -->|else + engine bootable| SM[smoke render on scratch copy]
  FT -->|red| FAIL[failed tool result + excerpt]
  SM -->|no render / captured error| FAIL
  FT -->|green| LAUNCH[launcher opens the app]
  SM -->|clean first render| LAUNCH
```
</details>

## preflight-review (review) — ok
Review delivered. Summary of the highest-impact findings:

- **BLOCKING**: The pre-flight gate is never wired in production — `agent_service_wiring.dart`'s `appLauncher` setter registers `openAppTool(env, launcher: launcher)` without `preflight:`, so the gate short-circuits to null and every production `open_app` succeeds unconditionally (AC7 inert). Additionally, no `FlutterTestRunner` implementation exists anywhere, making the AC10 flutter-test gate unreachable dead code outside tests.
- **IMPORTANT**: The scratch `MemoryExecutionEnv` isolates files but not the process-wide `_liveByApp` sibling-broadcast group, so a probe engine's storage writes reach real live engines of the same app; excerpts are unbounded (raw JS error text into the LLM-facing tool result, violating the bounded-payload AC); and the probe executes app JS with declared (not user-overridden) permissions, firing real network requests and diverging from the real launcher's exec semantics.
- **SUGGESTION**: iOS probe likely false-negatives (dlopen of system JSC is device-blocked) silently disabling the gate; cancelToken is never threaded through the gate; and the one-shot post-render error check misses asynchronously captured errors.

Conditional-import web safety, timer/listener hygiene, and the outcome-gating logic in `open_app_tool` were verified correct.
[Full output: agent://preflight-review]

## error-channel-review (review) — ok
Review complete. Summary of the 10 findings delivered to the orchestrator:

**BLOCKING (1):** The delivery path broadcasts to every live `AgentService` with no `appId`→session routing — one app error spawns a system-notice LLM turn in *all* open sessions, directly contradicting the channel's "exactly one owner … app-bound session" contract.

**IMPORTANT (4):**
- Engine boot failures never reach the channel (UI-only `_startError`; the `bootstrap` error kind has no emitter anywhere).
- `sourceRevision` hashes only the entry file — the circuit breaker never re-arms for helper-file fixes, and tile/app surfaces of one app double-report.
- The bootstrap JS never sends `fingerprint` (and no JS-side stack cap), so dedup is message-equality only — varying-message bursts bypass the gate entirely.
- `reportHostError` wraps only JSON→Widget conversion; actual Flutter inflation/layout errors (the red-screen ones) escape the try/catch.

**SUGGESTION (5):** misleading "may have been silenced" line on first notices; locale interpolation strips only `'` (syntax-error risk, not injectable); unguarded global assignments in the error-capture IIFE; unauthenticated `faAppError:` marker spoofing; unbounded smoke-gate error collector.

Also verified OK: revision captured at event time, breaker semantics, payload bounding, listener/subscription cleanup (no leaks), and publish reentrancy (async broadcast keeps `sendText` out of the build/log callback path).
[Full output: agent://error-channel-review]

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1246
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1246
- **Title**: gh-1164 [GOAL] built-in js-apps skill (promoted from app asset, decisive apps-vs-widget routing) + JS render/runtime errors reported back to the authoring agent as failures (blocked by #1151)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1164` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 106
- **Additions**: +4102
- **Deletions**: -165
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T21:23:19Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T21:37:25Z

## PR Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart
```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS[JS runtime throw] -->|faAppError log record| ENG[JsAppEngine]
  HOST[Flutter render build throw] -->|reportHostError| ENG
  ENG -->|gate + publish| GATE[JsAppErrorChannel]
  GATE -->|onDeliver| SVC[AgentService]
  SVC -->|sendText: mid-run steer / idle fresh turn| TURN[system-notice turn]
  OPEN[open_app tool] --> PF{preflight gate}
  PF -->|test file + runner| FT[flutter-test gate]
  PF -->|else + engine bootable| SM[smoke render on scratch copy]
  FT -->|red| FAIL[failed tool result + excerpt]
  SM -->|no render / captured error| FAIL
  FT -->|green| LAUNCH[launcher opens the app]
  SM -->|clean first render| LAUNCH
```
</details>

# pr-1246: gh-1164 [GOAL] built-in js-apps skill (promoted from app asset, decisive apps-vs-widget routing) + JS render/runtime errors reported back to the authoring agent as failures (blocked by #1151)

## Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart
```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS[JS runtime throw] -->|faAppError log record| ENG[JsAppEngine]
  HOST[Flutter render build throw] -->|reportHostError| ENG
  ENG -->|gate + publish| GATE[JsAppErrorChannel]
  GATE -->|onDeliver| SVC[AgentService]
  SVC -->|sendText: mid-run steer / idle fresh turn| TURN[system-notice turn]
  OPEN[open_app tool] --> PF{preflight gate}
  PF -->|test file + runner| FT[flutter-test gate]
  PF -->|else + engine bootable| SM[smoke render on scratch copy]
  FT -->|red| FAIL[failed tool result + excerpt]
  SM -->|no render / captured error| FAIL
  FT -->|green| LAUNCH[launcher opens the app]
  SM -->|clean first render| LAUNCH
```
</details>

## preflight-review (review) — ok
Review delivered. Summary of the highest-impact findings:

- **BLOCKING**: The pre-flight gate is never wired in production — `agent_service_wiring.dart`'s `appLauncher` setter registers `openAppTool(env, launcher: launcher)` without `preflight:`, so the gate short-circuits to null and every production `open_app` succeeds unconditionally (AC7 inert). Additionally, no `FlutterTestRunner` implementation exists anywhere, making the AC10 flutter-test gate unreachable dead code outside tests.
- **IMPORTANT**: The scratch `MemoryExecutionEnv` isolates files but not the process-wide `_liveByApp` sibling-broadcast group, so a probe engine's storage writes reach real live engines of the same app; excerpts are unbounded (raw JS error text into the LLM-facing tool result, violating the bounded-payload AC); and the probe executes app JS with declared (not user-overridden) permissions, firing real network requests and diverging from the real launcher's exec semantics.
- **SUGGESTION**: iOS probe likely false-negatives (dlopen of system JSC is device-blocked) silently disabling the gate; cancelToken is never threaded through the gate; and the one-shot post-render error check misses asynchronously captured errors.

Conditional-import web safety, timer/listener hygiene, and the outcome-gating logic in `open_app_tool` were verified correct.
[Full output: agent://preflight-review]

## error-channel-review (review) — ok
Review complete. Summary of the 10 findings delivered to the orchestrator:

**BLOCKING (1):** The delivery path broadcasts to every live `AgentService` with no `appId`→session routing — one app error spawns a system-notice LLM turn in *all* open sessions, directly contradicting the channel's "exactly one owner … app-bound session" contract.

**IMPORTANT (4):**
- Engine boot failures never reach the channel (UI-only `_startError`; the `bootstrap` error kind has no emitter anywhere).
- `sourceRevision` hashes only the entry file — the circuit breaker never re-arms for helper-file fixes, and tile/app surfaces of one app double-report.
- The bootstrap JS never sends `fingerprint` (and no JS-side stack cap), so dedup is message-equality only — varying-message bursts bypass the gate entirely.
- `reportHostError` wraps only JSON→Widget conversion; actual Flutter inflation/layout errors (the red-screen ones) escape the try/catch.

**SUGGESTION (5):** misleading "may have been silenced" line on first notices; locale interpolation strips only `'` (syntax-error risk, not injectable); unguarded global assignments in the error-capture IIFE; unauthenticated `faAppError:` marker spoofing; unbounded smoke-gate error collector.

Also verified OK: revision captured at event time, breaker semantics, payload bounding, listener/subscription cleanup (no leaks), and publish reentrancy (async broadcast keeps `sendText` out of the build/log callback path).
[Full output: agent://error-channel-review]

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1246
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1246
- **Title**: gh-1164 [GOAL] built-in js-apps skill (promoted from app asset, decisive apps-vs-widget routing) + JS render/runtime errors reported back to the authoring agent as failures (blocked by #1151)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1164` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 106
- **Additions**: +4102
- **Deletions**: -165
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T21:23:19Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T21:37:25Z

## PR Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart
```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS[JS runtime throw] -->|faAppError log record| ENG[JsAppEngine]
  HOST[Flutter render build throw] -->|reportHostError| ENG
  ENG -->|gate + publish| GATE[JsAppErrorChannel]
  GATE -->|onDeliver| SVC[AgentService]
  SVC -->|sendText: mid-run steer / idle fresh turn| TURN[system-notice turn]
  OPEN[open_app tool] --> PF{preflight gate}
  PF -->|test file + runner| FT[flutter-test gate]
  PF -->|else + engine bootable| SM[smoke render on scratch copy]
  FT -->|red| FAIL[failed tool result + excerpt]
  SM -->|no render / captured error| FAIL
  FT -->|green| LAUNCH[launcher opens the app]
  SM -->|clean first render| LAUNCH
```
</details>

Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1246
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1246
- **Title**: gh-1164 [GOAL] built-in js-apps skill (promoted from app asset, decisive apps-vs-widget routing) + JS render/runtime errors reported back to the authoring agent as failures (blocked by #1151)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1164` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 106
- **Additions**: +4102
- **Deletions**: -165
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T21:23:19Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T21:37:25Z

## PR Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart
```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS[JS runtime throw] -->|faAppError log record| ENG[JsAppEngine]
  HOST[Flutter render build throw] -->|reportHostError| ENG
  ENG -->|gate + publish| GATE[JsAppErrorChannel]
  GATE -->|onDeliver| SVC[AgentService]
  SVC -->|sendText: mid-run steer / idle fresh turn| TURN[system-notice turn]
  OPEN[open_app tool] --> PF{preflight gate}
  PF -->|test file + runner| FT[flutter-test gate]
  PF -->|else + engine bootable| SM[smoke render on scratch copy]
  FT -->|red| FAIL[failed tool result + excerpt]
  SM -->|no render / captured error| FAIL
  FT -->|green| LAUNCH[launcher opens the app]
  SM -->|clean first render| LAUNCH
```
</details>

# pr-1246: gh-1164 [GOAL] built-in js-apps skill (promoted from app asset, decisive apps-vs-widget routing) + JS render/runtime errors reported back to the authoring agent as failures (blocked by #1151)

## Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart
```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS[JS runtime throw] -->|faAppError log record| ENG[JsAppEngine]
  HOST[Flutter render build throw] -->|reportHostError| ENG
  ENG -->|gate + publish| GATE[JsAppErrorChannel]
  GATE -->|onDeliver| SVC[AgentService]
  SVC -->|sendText: mid-run steer / idle fresh turn| TURN[system-notice turn]
  OPEN[open_app tool] --> PF{preflight gate}
  PF -->|test file + runner| FT[flutter-test gate]
  PF -->|else + engine bootable| SM[smoke render on scratch copy]
  FT -->|red| FAIL[failed tool result + excerpt]
  SM -->|no render / captured error| FAIL
  FT -->|green| LAUNCH[launcher opens the app]
  SM -->|clean first render| LAUNCH
```
</details>

- **IMPORTANT**: The scratch `MemoryExecutionEnv` isolates files but not the process-wide `_liveByApp` sibling-broadcast group, so a probe engine's storage writes reach real live engines of the same app; excerpts are unbounded (raw JS error text into the LLM-facing tool result, violating the bounded-payload AC); and the probe executes app JS with declared (not user-overridden) permissions, firing real network requests and diverging from the real launcher's exec semantics.
- **SUGGESTION**: iOS probe likely false-negatives (dlopen of system JSC is device-blocked) silently disabling the gate; cancelToken is never threaded through the gate; and the one-shot post-render error check misses asynchronously captured errors.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1246
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1246
- **Title**: gh-1164 [GOAL] built-in js-apps skill (promoted from app asset, decisive apps-vs-widget routing) + JS render/runtime errors reported back to the authoring agent as failures (blocked by #1151)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1164` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 106
- **Additions**: +4102
- **Deletions**: -165
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T21:23:19Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T21:37:25Z

## PR Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart
```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS[JS runtime throw] -->|faAppError log record| ENG[JsAppEngine]
  HOST[Flutter render build throw] -->|reportHostError| ENG
  ENG -->|gate + publish| GATE[JsAppErrorChannel]
  GATE -->|onDeliver| SVC[AgentService]
  SVC -->|sendText: mid-run steer / idle fresh turn| TURN[system-notice turn]
  OPEN[open_app tool] --> PF{preflight gate}
  PF -->|test file + runner| FT[flutter-test gate]
  PF -->|else + engine bootable| SM[smoke render on scratch copy]
  FT -->|red| FAIL[failed tool result + excerpt]
  SM -->|no render / captured error| FAIL
  FT -->|green| LAUNCH[launcher opens the app]
  SM -->|clean first render| LAUNCH
```
</details>

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1246
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1246
- **Title**: gh-1164 [GOAL] built-in js-apps skill (promoted from app asset, decisive apps-vs-widget routing) + JS render/runtime errors reported back to the authoring agent as failures (blocked by #1151)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1164` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 106
- **Additions**: +4102
- **Deletions**: -165
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T21:23:19Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T21:37:25Z

## PR Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart
```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS[JS runtime throw] -->|faAppError log record| ENG[JsAppEngine]
  HOST[Flutter render build throw] -->|reportHostError| ENG
  ENG -->|gate + publish| GATE[JsAppErrorChannel]
  GATE -->|onDeliver| SVC[AgentService]
  SVC -->|sendText: mid-run steer / idle fresh turn| TURN[system-notice turn]
  OPEN[open_app tool] --> PF{preflight gate}
  PF -->|test file + runner| FT[flutter-test gate]
  PF -->|else + engine bootable| SM[smoke render on scratch copy]
  FT -->|red| FAIL[failed tool result + excerpt]
  SM -->|no render / captured error| FAIL
  FT -->|green| LAUNCH[launcher opens the app]
  SM -->|clean first render| LAUNCH
```
</details>

# pr-1246: gh-1164 [GOAL] built-in js-apps skill (promoted from app asset, decisive apps-vs-widget routing) + JS render/runtime errors reported back to the authoring agent as failures (blocked by #1151)

## Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart
```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS[JS runtime throw] -->|faAppError log record| ENG[JsAppEngine]
  HOST[Flutter render build throw] -->|reportHostError| ENG
  ENG -->|gate + publish| GATE[JsAppErrorChannel]
  GATE -->|onDeliver| SVC[AgentService]
  SVC -->|sendText: mid-run steer / idle fresh turn| TURN[system-notice turn]
  OPEN[open_app tool] --> PF{preflight gate}
  PF -->|test file + runner| FT[flutter-test gate]
  PF -->|else + engine bootable| SM[smoke render on scratch copy]
  FT -->|red| FAIL[failed tool result + excerpt]
  SM -->|no render / captured error| FAIL
  FT -->|green| LAUNCH[launcher opens the app]
  SM -->|clean first render| LAUNCH
```
</details>

## preflight-review (review) — ok
Review delivered. Summary of the highest-impact findings:

- **BLOCKING**: The pre-flight gate is never wired in production — `agent_service_wiring.dart`'s `appLauncher` setter registers `openAppTool(env, launcher: launcher)` without `preflight:`, so the gate short-circuits to null and every production `open_app` succeeds unconditionally (AC7 inert). Additionally, no `FlutterTestRunner` implementation exists anywhere, making the AC10 flutter-test gate unreachable dead code outside tests.
- **IMPORTANT**: The scratch `MemoryExecutionEnv` isolates files but not the process-wide `_liveByApp` sibling-broadcast group, so a probe engine's storage writes reach real live engines of the same app; excerpts are unbounded (raw JS error text into the LLM-facing tool result, violating the bounded-payload AC); and the probe executes app JS with declared (not user-overridden) permissions, firing real network requests and diverging from the real launcher's exec semantics.
- **SUGGESTION**: iOS probe likely false-negatives (dlopen of system JSC is device-blocked) silently disabling the gate; cancelToken is never threaded through the gate; and the one-shot post-render error check misses asynchronously captured errors.

Conditional-import web safety, timer/listener hygiene, and the outcome-gating logic in `open_app_tool` were verified correct.

## error-channel-review (review) — ok
Review complete. Summary of the 10 findings delivered to the orchestrator:

**BLOCKING (1):** The delivery path broadcasts to every live `AgentService` with no `appId`→session routing — one app error spawns a system-notice LLM turn in *all* open sessions, directly contradicting the channel's "exactly one owner … app-bound session" contract.

**IMPORTANT (4):**
- Engine boot failures never reach the channel (UI-only `_startError`; the `bootstrap` error kind has no emitter anywhere).
- `sourceRevision` hashes only the entry file — the circuit breaker never re-arms for helper-file fixes, and tile/app surfaces of one app double-report.
- The bootstrap JS never sends `fingerprint` (and no JS-side stack cap), so dedup is message-equality only — varying-message bursts bypass the gate entirely.
- `reportHostError` wraps only JSON→Widget conversion; actual Flutter inflation/layout errors (the red-screen ones) escape the try/catch.

**SUGGESTION (5):** misleading "may have been silenced" line on first notices; locale interpolation strips only `'` (syntax-error risk, not injectable); unguarded global assignments in the error-capture IIFE; unauthenticated `faAppError:` marker spoofing; unbounded smoke-gate error collector.

Also verified OK: revision captured at event time, breaker semantics, payload bounding, listener/subscription cleanup (no leaks), and publish reentrancy (async broadcast keeps `sendText` out of the build/log callback path).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1246

- **Title**: gh-1164 [GOAL] built-in js-apps skill (promoted from app asset, decisive apps-vs-widget routing) + JS render/runtime errors reported back to the authoring agent as failures (blocked by #1151)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1164` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 106
- **Additions**: +4102
- **Deletions**: -165
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T21:23:19Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T21:37:25Z

## PR Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart
```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS[JS runtime throw] -->|faAppError log record| ENG[JsAppEngine]
  HOST[Flutter render build throw] -->|reportHostError| ENG
  ENG -->|gate + publish| GATE[JsAppErrorChannel]
  GATE -->|onDeliver| SVC[AgentService]
  SVC -->|sendText: mid-run steer / idle fresh turn| TURN[system-notice turn]
  OPEN[open_app tool] --> PF{preflight gate}
  PF -->|test file + runner| FT[flutter-test gate]
  PF -->|else + engine bootable| SM[smoke render on scratch copy]
  FT -->|red| FAIL[failed tool result + excerpt]
  SM -->|no render / captured error| FAIL
  FT -->|green| LAUNCH[launcher opens the app]
  SM -->|clean first render| LAUNCH
```
</details>

## PR Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart

Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

## preflight-review (review) — ok
Review delivered. Summary of the highest-impact findings:

- **BLOCKING**: The pre-flight gate is never wired in production — `agent_service_wiring.dart`'s `appLauncher` setter registers `openAppTool(env, launcher: launcher)` without `preflight:`, so the gate short-circuits to null and every production `open_app` succeeds unconditionally (AC7 inert). Additionally, no `FlutterTestRunner` implementation exists anywhere, making the AC10 flutter-test gate unreachable dead code outside tests.
- **IMPORTANT**: The scratch `MemoryExecutionEnv` isolates files but not the process-wide `_liveByApp` sibling-broadcast group, so a probe engine's storage writes reach real live engines of the same app; excerpts are unbounded (raw JS error text into the LLM-facing tool result, violating the bounded-payload AC); and the probe executes app JS with declared (not user-overridden) permissions, firing real network requests and diverging from the real launcher's exec semantics.
- **SUGGESTION**: iOS probe likely false-negatives (dlopen of system JSC is device-blocked) silently disabling the gate; cancelToken is never threaded through the gate; and the one-shot post-render error check misses asynchronously captured errors.

Conditional-import web safety, timer/listener hygiene, and the outcome-gating logic in `open_app_tool` were verified correct.
[Full output: agent://preflight-review]

## error-channel-review (review) — ok
Review complete. Summary of the 10 findings delivered to the orchestrator:

**BLOCKING (1):** The delivery path broadcasts to every live `AgentService` with no `appId`→session routing — one app error spawns a system-notice LLM turn in *all* open sessions, directly contradicting the channel's "exactly one owner … app-bound session" contract.

**IMPORTANT (4):**
- Engine boot failures never reach the channel (UI-only `_startError`; the `bootstrap` error kind has no emitter anywhere).
- `sourceRevision` hashes only the entry file — the circuit breaker never re-arms for helper-file fixes, and tile/app surfaces of one app double-report.
- The bootstrap JS never sends `fingerprint` (and no JS-side stack cap), so dedup is message-equality only — varying-message bursts bypass the gate entirely.
- `reportHostError` wraps only JSON→Widget conversion; actual Flutter inflation/layout errors (the red-screen ones) escape the try/catch.

**SUGGESTION (5):** misleading "may have been silenced" line on first notices; locale interpolation strips only `'` (syntax-error risk, not injectable); unguarded global assignments in the error-capture IIFE; unauthenticated `faAppError:` marker spoofing; unbounded smoke-gate error collector.

Also verified OK: revision captured at event time, breaker semantics, payload bounding, listener/subscription cleanup (no leaks), and publish reentrancy (async broadcast keeps `sendText` out of the build/log callback path).
[Full output: agent://error-channel-review]

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1246
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1246
- **Title**: gh-1164 [GOAL] built-in js-apps skill (promoted from app asset, decisive apps-vs-widget routing) + JS render/runtime errors reported back to the authoring agent as failures (blocked by #1151)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1164` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 106
- **Additions**: +4102
- **Deletions**: -165
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T21:23:19Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T21:37:25Z

## PR Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart
```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS[JS runtime throw] -->|faAppError log record| ENG[JsAppEngine]
  HOST[Flutter render build throw] -->|reportHostError| ENG
  ENG -->|gate + publish| GATE[JsAppErrorChannel]
  GATE -->|onDeliver| SVC[AgentService]
  SVC -->|sendText: mid-run steer / idle fresh turn| TURN[system-notice turn]
  OPEN[open_app tool] --> PF{preflight gate}
  PF -->|test file + runner| FT[flutter-test gate]
  PF -->|else + engine bootable| SM[smoke render on scratch copy]
  FT -->|red| FAIL[failed tool result + excerpt]
  SM -->|no render / captured error| FAIL
  FT -->|green| LAUNCH[launcher opens the app]
  SM -->|clean first render| LAUNCH
```
</details>

- **IMPORTANT**: The scratch `MemoryExecutionEnv` isolates files but not the process-wide `_liveByApp` sibling-broadcast group, so a probe engine's storage writes reach real live engines of the same app; excerpts are unbounded (raw JS error text into the LLM-facing tool result, violating the bounded-payload AC); and the probe executes app JS with declared (not user-overridden) permissions, firing real network requests and diverging from the real launcher's exec semantics.

## error-channel-review (review) — ok
Review complete. Summary of the 10 findings delivered to the orchestrator:

**BLOCKING (1):** The delivery path broadcasts to every live `AgentService` with no `appId`→session routing — one app error spawns a system-notice LLM turn in *all* open sessions, directly contradicting the channel's "exactly one owner … app-bound session" contract.

**IMPORTANT (4):**
- Engine boot failures never reach the channel (UI-only `_startError`; the `bootstrap` error kind has no emitter anywhere).
- `sourceRevision` hashes only the entry file — the circuit breaker never re-arms for helper-file fixes, and tile/app surfaces of one app double-report.

Confirmed the channel doc says "exactly one owner (AgentService) subscribes onDeliver and routes notices into the app-bound session" — but the actual wiring in agent_service.dart listens on EVERY AgentService instance, and `_onJsAppError` does NOT filter by appId or route to an app-bound session — every session gets a system notice turn for any app's error. That is a genuine design/behavior gap vs the contract. Is it BLOCKING or IMPORTANT? The PR description claims "delivers a system notice into the bound session". The AC presumably requires the notice to reach the authoring agent. Broadcasting to all sessions means: a user with N sessions open gets N spurious LLM turns (each costing tokens, potentially acting on an unrelated app's error). This is a real correctness issue — an error in app A generates a steer/turn in every other session, where the agent may react to an error of an app it never touched. That can cause wrong behavior (agents "fixing" things not theirs). I'd rate IMPORTANT-to-BLOCKING. Per "when in doubt, start one level higher" — but CI already gives us blocking items and recommendation REQUEST_CHANGES. Broadcasting wrong-session notices is a correctness bug in a core feature of this PR; I'll rate it BLOCKING... hmm. Let me think: the notice goes to all live AgentServices. In a single-session host (typical app use), it's fine. In multi-session (sessions list exists in the app), each session's agent gets a system notice about an unrelated app. The agent in session B has no context about app A; it may start a fresh turn and do things. This is a real bug against the PR's own stated contract. I'll mark it BLOCKING? The verdict rules: BLOCKING = broken behavior. Multi-session delivery to the wrong session is broken behavior of the feature. But severity inflation... The machine: REQUEST_CHANGES already due to CI. Adding another blocking is fine. I'll classify as IMPORTANT... Let me decide: the contract explicitly says "exactly one owner ... routes notices into the app-bound session". The implementation doesn't route at all. In the common single-session case behavior matches expectations; in multi-session it's wrong and wasteful. I'll go with IMPORTANT (real correctness gap, works as shipped in the common case). Hmm, but "when in doubt, start one level higher". Doubt exists → BLOCKING? The instruction says classify: BLOCKING = merge would cause a bug. Multi-session wrong-recipient notices IS a bug caused by merging. I'll go BLOCKING. Actually let me reconsider — the authoring-agent story: apps are authored within a session; other sessions receiving the notice get a system-notice they didn't ask for, and sendText starts a FRESH TURN in idle sessions — agents burning tokens/actions on unrelated errors. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1246
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1246
- **Title**: gh-1164 [GOAL] built-in js-apps skill (promoted from app asset, decisive apps-vs-widget routing) + JS render/runtime errors reported back to the authoring agent as failures (blocked by #1151)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1164` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 106
- **Additions**: +4102
- **Deletions**: -165
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T21:23:19Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T21:37:25Z

## PR Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart
```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS[JS runtime throw] -->|faAppError log record| ENG[JsAppEngine]
  HOST[Flutter render build throw] -->|reportHostError| ENG
  ENG -->|gate + publish| GATE[JsAppErrorChannel]
  GATE -->|onDeliver| SVC[AgentService]
  SVC -->|sendText: mid-run steer / idle fresh turn| TURN[system-notice turn]
  OPEN[open_app tool] --> PF{preflight gate}
  PF -->|test file + runner| FT[flutter-test gate]
  PF -->|else + engine bootable| SM[smoke render on scratch copy]
  FT -->|red| FAIL[failed tool result + excerpt]
  SM -->|no render / captured error| FAIL
  FT -->|green| LAUNCH[launcher opens the app]
  SM -->|clean first render| LAUNCH
```
</details>

That is a genuine design/behavior gap vs the contract. Is it BLOCKING or IMPORTANT? The PR description claims "delivers a system notice into the bound session". The AC presumably requires the notice to reach the authoring agent. Broadcasting to all sessions means: a user with N sessions open gets N spurious LLM turns (each costing tokens, potentially acting on an unrelated app's error). This is a real correctness issue — an error in app A generates a steer/turn in every other session, where the agent may react to an error of an app it never touched. That can cause wrong behavior (agents "fixing" things not theirs). I'd rate IMPORTANT-to-BLOCKING. Per "when in doubt, start one level higher" — but CI already gives us blocking items and recommendation REQUEST_CHANGES. Broadcasting wrong-session notices is a correctness bug in a core feature of this PR; I'll rate it BLOCKING... hmm. Let me think: the notice goes to all live AgentServices. In a single-session host (typical app use), it's fine. In multi-session (sessions list exists in the app), each session's agent gets a system notice about an unrelated app. The agent in session B has no context about app A; it may start a fresh turn and do things. This is a real bug against the PR's own stated contract. I'll mark it BLOCKING? The verdict rules: BLOCKING = broken behavior. Actually let me reconsider — the authoring-agent story: apps are authored within a session; other sessions receiving the notice get a system-notice they didn't ask for, and sendText starts a FRESH TURN in idle sessions — agents burning tokens/actions on unrelated errors. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,

callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4.
