# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1246
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1246
- **Title**: gh-1164 [GOAL] built-in js-apps skill (promoted from app asset, decisive apps-vs-widget routing) + JS render/runtime errors reported back to the authoring agent as failures (blocked by #1151)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1164` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 106
- **Additions**: +4102
- **Deletions**: -165
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T21:23:19Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T21:37:25Z

## PR Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart
```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS[JS runtime throw] -->|faAppError log record| ENG[JsAppEngine]
  HOST[Flutter render build throw] -->|reportHostError| ENG
  ENG -->|gate + publish| GATE[JsAppErrorChannel]
  GATE -->|onDeliver| SVC[AgentService]
  SVC -->|sendText: mid-run steer / idle fresh turn| TURN[system-notice turn]
  OPEN[open_app tool] --> PF{preflight gate}
  PF -->|test file + runner| FT[flutter-test gate]
  PF -->|else + engine bootable| SM[smoke render on scratch copy]
  FT -->|red| FAIL[failed tool result + excerpt]
  SM -->|no render / captured error| FAIL
  FT -->|green| LAUNCH[launcher opens the app]
  SM -->|clean first render| LAUNCH
```
</details>

Broadcasting to all sessions means: a user with N sessions open gets N spurious LLM turns (each costing tokens, potentially acting on an unrelated app's error). This is a real correctness issue — an error in app A generates a steer/turn in every other session, where the agent may react to an error of an app it never touched. That can cause wrong behavior (agents "fixing" things not theirs). I'd rate IMPORTANT-to-BLOCKING. Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. - **Author**: ai-teammate

- **State**: open

- **Deletions**: -165

- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T21:37:25Z

## PR Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart
```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

  PF -->|else + engine bootable| SM[smoke render on scratch copy]

```

Confirmed the channel doc says "exactly one owner (AgentService) subscribes onDeliver and routes notices into the app-bound session" — but the actual wiring in agent_service.dart listens on EVERY AgentService instance, and `_onJsAppError` does NOT filter by appId or route to an app-bound session — every session gets a system notice turn for any app's error. That is a genuine design/behavior gap vs the contract. Is it BLOCKING or IMPORTANT? The PR description claims "delivers a system notice into the bound session". The AC presumably requires the notice to reach the authoring agent. Broadcasting to all sessions means: a user with N sessions open gets N spurious LLM turns (each costing tokens, potentially acting on an unrelated app's error). This is a real correctness issue — an error in app A generates a steer/turn in every other session, where the agent may react to an error of an app it never touched. That can cause wrong behavior (agents "fixing" things not theirs). I'd rate IMPORTANT-to-BLOCKING. Per "when in doubt, start one level higher" — but CI already gives us blocking items and recommendation REQUEST_CHANGES. re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1246
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1246
- **Title**: gh-1164 [GOAL] built-in js-apps skill (promoted from app asset, decisive apps-vs-widget routing) + JS render/runtime errors reported back to the authoring agent as failures (blocked by #1151)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1164` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 106
- **Additions**: +4102
- **Deletions**: -165
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T21:23:19Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T21:37:25Z

## PR Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart
```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS[JS runtime throw] -->|faAppError log record| ENG[JsAppEngine]
  HOST[Flutter render build throw] -->|reportHostError| ENG
  ENG -->|gate + publish| GATE[JsAppErrorChannel]
  GATE -->|onDeliver| SVC[AgentService]
  SVC -->|sendText: mid-run steer / idle fresh turn| TURN[system-notice turn]
  OPEN[open_app tool] --> PF{preflight gate}
  PF -->|test file + runner| FT[flutter-test gate]
  PF -->|else + engine bootable| SM[smoke render on scratch copy]
  FT -->|red| FAIL[failed tool result + excerpt]
  SM -->|no render / captured error| FAIL
  FT -->|green| LAUNCH[launcher opens the app]
  SM -->|clean first render| LAUNCH
```
</details>

BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1246
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1246
- **Title**: gh-1164 [GOAL] built-in js-apps skill (promoted from app asset, decisive apps-vs-widget routing) + JS render/runtime errors reported back to the authoring agent as failures (blocked by #1151)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1164` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 106
- **Additions**: +4102
- **Deletions**: -165
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T21:23:19Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T21:37:25Z

## PR Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart
```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS[JS runtime throw] -->|faAppError log record| ENG[JsAppEngine]
  HOST[Flutter render build throw] -->|reportHostError| ENG
  ENG -->|gate + publish| GATE[JsAppErrorChannel]
  GATE -->|onDeliver| SVC[AgentService]
  SVC -->|sendText: mid-run steer / idle fresh turn| TURN[system-notice turn]
  OPEN[open_app tool] --> PF{preflight gate}
  PF -->|test file + runner| FT[flutter-test gate]
  PF -->|else + engine bootable| SM[smoke render on scratch copy]
  FT -->|red| FAIL[failed tool result + excerpt]
  SM -->|no render / captured error| FAIL
  FT -->|green| LAUNCH[launcher opens the app]
  SM -->|clean first render| LAUNCH
```
</details>

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. - **Author**: ai-teammate

- **State**: open

- **Deletions**: -165

- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T21:37:25Z

## PR Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart
```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

  PF -->|else + engine bootable| SM[smoke render on scratch copy]

```

Confirmed the channel doc says "exactly one owner (AgentService) subscribes onDeliver and routes notices into the app-bound session" — but the actual wiring in agent_service.dart listens on EVERY AgentService instance, and `_onJsAppError` does NOT filter by appId or route to an app-bound session — every session gets a system notice turn for any app's error. That is a genuine design/behavior gap vs the contract. Is it BLOCKING or IMPORTANT? The PR description claims "delivers a system notice into the bound session". The AC presumably requires the notice to reach the authoring agent. Broadcasting to all sessions means: a user with N sessions open gets N spurious LLM turns (each costing tokens, potentially acting on an unrelated app's error). This is a real correctness issue — an error in app A generates a steer/turn in every other session, where the agent may react to an error of an app it never touched. That can cause wrong behavior (agents "fixing" things not theirs). I'd rate IMPORTANT-to-BLOCKING. Per "when in doubt, start one level higher" — but CI already gives us blocking items and recommendation REQUEST_CHANGES. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1246
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1246
- **Title**: gh-1164 [GOAL] built-in js-apps skill (promoted from app asset, decisive apps-vs-widget routing) + JS render/runtime errors reported back to the authoring agent as failures (blocked by #1151)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1164` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 106
- **Additions**: +4102
- **Deletions**: -165
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T21:23:19Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T21:37:25Z

## PR Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart
```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS[JS runtime throw] -->|faAppError log record| ENG[JsAppEngine]
  HOST[Flutter render build throw] -->|reportHostError| ENG
  ENG -->|gate + publish| GATE[JsAppErrorChannel]
  GATE -->|onDeliver| SVC[AgentService]
  SVC -->|sendText: mid-run steer / idle fresh turn| TURN[system-notice turn]
  OPEN[open_app tool] --> PF{preflight gate}
  PF -->|test file + runner| FT[flutter-test gate]
  PF -->|else + engine bootable| SM[smoke render on scratch copy]
  FT -->|red| FAIL[failed tool result + excerpt]
  SM -->|no render / captured error| FAIL
  FT -->|green| LAUNCH[launcher opens the app]
  SM -->|clean first render| LAUNCH
```
</details>

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1246
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1246
- **Title**: gh-1164 [GOAL] built-in js-apps skill (promoted from app asset, decisive apps-vs-widget routing) + JS render/runtime errors reported back to the authoring agent as failures (blocked by #1151)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1164` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 106
- **Additions**: +4102
- **Deletions**: -165
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T21:23:19Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T21:37:25Z

## PR Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart
```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS[JS runtime throw] -->|faAppError log record| ENG[JsAppEngine]
  HOST[Flutter render build throw] -->|reportHostError| ENG
  ENG -->|gate + publish| GATE[JsAppErrorChannel]
  GATE -->|onDeliver| SVC[AgentService]
  SVC -->|sendText: mid-run steer / idle fresh turn| TURN[system-notice turn]
  OPEN[open_app tool] --> PF{preflight gate}
  PF -->|test file + runner| FT[flutter-test gate]
  PF -->|else + engine bootable| SM[smoke render on scratch copy]
  FT -->|red| FAIL[failed tool result + excerpt]
  SM -->|no render / captured error| FAIL
  FT -->|green| LAUNCH[launcher opens the app]
  SM -->|clean first render| LAUNCH
```
</details>

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1246
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1246
- **Title**: gh-1164 [GOAL] built-in js-apps skill (promoted from app asset, decisive apps-vs-widget routing) + JS render/runtime errors reported back to the authoring agent as failures (blocked by #1151)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1164` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 106
- **Additions**: +4102
- **Deletions**: -165
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T21:23:19Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T21:37:25Z

## PR Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart
```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS[JS runtime throw] -->|faAppError log record| ENG[JsAppEngine]
  HOST[Flutter render build throw] -->|reportHostError| ENG
  ENG -->|gate + publish| GATE[JsAppErrorChannel]
  GATE -->|onDeliver| SVC[AgentService]
  SVC -->|sendText: mid-run steer / idle fresh turn| TURN[system-notice turn]
  OPEN[open_app tool] --> PF{preflight gate}
  PF -->|test file + runner| FT[flutter-test gate]
  PF -->|else + engine bootable| SM[smoke render on scratch copy]
  FT -->|red| FAIL[failed tool result + excerpt]
  SM -->|no render / captured error| FAIL
  FT -->|green| LAUNCH[launcher opens the app]
  SM -->|clean first render| LAUNCH
```
</details>

Confirmed the channel doc says "exactly one owner (AgentService) subscribes onDeliver and routes notices into the app-bound session" — but the actual wiring in agent_service.dart listens on EVERY AgentService instance, and `_onJsAppError` does NOT filter by appId or route to an app-bound session — every session gets a system notice turn for any app's error. That is a genuine design/behavior gap vs the contract. Is it BLOCKING or IMPORTANT? The PR description claims "delivers a system notice into the bound session". The AC presumably requires the notice to reach the authoring agent. Broadcasting to all sessions means: a user with N sessions open gets N spurious LLM turns (each costing tokens, potentially acting on an unrelated app's error). This is a real correctness issue — an error in app A generates a steer/turn in every other session, where the agent may react to an error of an app it never touched. That can cause wrong behavior (agents "fixing" things not theirs). I'd rate IMPORTANT-to-BLOCKING. Per "when in doubt, start one level higher" — but CI already gives us blocking items and recommendation REQUEST_CHANGES. Broadcasting wrong-session notices is a correctness bug in a core feature of this PR; I'll rate it BLOCKING... hmm. Let me think: the notice goes to all live AgentServices. In a single-session host (typical app use), it's fine. In multi-session (sessions list exists in the app), each session's agent gets a system notice about an unrelated app. The agent in session B has no context about app A; it may start a fresh turn and do things. This is a real bug against the PR's own stated contract. I'll mark it BLOCKING? The verdict rules: BLOCKING = broken behavior. Multi-session delivery to the wrong session is broken behavior of the feature. But severity inflation... The machine: REQUEST_CHANGES already due to CI. Adding another blocking is fine. I'll classify as IMPORTANT... Let me decide: the contract explicitly says "exactly one owner ... routes notices into the app-bound session". The implementation doesn't route at all. In the common single-session case behavior matches expectations; in multi-session it's wrong and wasteful. I'll go with IMPORTANT (real correctness gap, works as shipped in the common case). Hmm, but "when in doubt, start one level higher". Doubt exists → BLOCKING? The instruction says classify: BLOCKING = merge would cause a bug. Multi-session wrong-recipient notices IS a bug caused by merging. I'll go BLOCKING. Actually let me reconsider — the authoring-agent story: apps are authored within a session; other sessions receiving the notice get a system-notice they didn't ask for, and sendText starts a FRESH TURN in idle sessions — agents burning tokens/actions on unrelated errors. In a product where autonomous agents act on system notices, this is a genuine bug. BLOCKING.

Now the other subagent findings — spot-check a few more:

1. error-channel IMPORTANT: "Engine boot failures never reach the channel (UI-only _startError; the bootstrap error kind has no emitter)". PR description says "Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3...)" — that's a documented decision, so NOT a finding. The subagent may have missed this. Skip/downgrade.

2. "sourceRevision hashes only the entry file" — need verification. Check js_app_errors.dart / engine sourceRevision.

3. "bootstrap JS never sends fingerprint → dedup is message-equality only" — check JsAppErrorEvent.dedupKey.

4. preflight IMPORTANT: scratch env storage broadcast group — check _liveByApp / MemoryExecutionEnv.

5. preflight IMPORTANT: unbounded excerpt — check open_app_tool excerpt handling.

6. preflight: no FlutterTestRunner production impl — verify via grep. The PR says "when the toolchain exists" — is there any real runner? grep FlutterTestRunner across repo.

7. skill-promotion suggestions: doc-rot items — verify quickly.

Burst errors with varying messages (e.g., animation frame errors including numbers/timestamps) bypass dedup → each variant delivered as a notice → up to breakerThreshold (5) notices per key... actually per distinct key, so a burst of varying messages = many notices → breaker only silences after 5 of the SAME key. PR claims "one report per app+fingerprint". IMPORTANT.

Since the smoke engine boots on a scratch copy of files but storage broadcasts bypass the env... Let me check _broadcastStorageChanges — does it write to env or broadcast in-memory? {"command":"sed -n 514,580p flutter_app/lib/apps/js_app_engine.dart"}

Confirmed: the smoke gate's probe engine joins `_liveByApp[app.id]`, and any `jsr.storage.set` during the probe's headless run broadcasts `state.sync` to the app's real live engines (tile/fullscreen), mutating the live UI's in-memory state from a throwaway pre-flight probe. Also reverse: a live engine write during the probe gets replayed. The gate's scratch-copy claim ("never touch the app's real files or storage") is thus violated through the process-wide sibling broadcast. This is a genuine IMPORTANT finding (probe side effects leak into the live app).

surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1246
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1246
- **Title**: gh-1164 [GOAL] built-in js-apps skill (promoted from app asset, decisive apps-vs-widget routing) + JS render/runtime errors reported back to the authoring agent as failures (blocked by #1151)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1164` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 106
- **Additions**: +4102
- **Deletions**: -165
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T21:23:19Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T21:37:25Z

## PR Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart
```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS[JS runtime throw] -->|faAppError log record| ENG[JsAppEngine]
  HOST[Flutter render build throw] -->|reportHostError| ENG
  ENG -->|gate + publish| GATE[JsAppErrorChannel]
  GATE -->|onDeliver| SVC[AgentService]
  SVC -->|sendText: mid-run steer / idle fresh turn| TURN[system-notice turn]
  OPEN[open_app tool] --> PF{preflight gate}
  PF -->|test file + runner| FT[flutter-test gate]
  PF -->|else + engine bootable| SM[smoke render on scratch copy]
  FT -->|red| FAIL[failed tool result + excerpt]
  SM -->|no render / captured error| FAIL
  FT -->|green| LAUNCH[launcher opens the app]
  SM -->|clean first render| LAUNCH
```
</details>

# pr-1246: gh-1164 [GOAL] built-in js-apps skill (promoted from app asset, decisive apps-vs-widget routing) + JS render/runtime errors reported back to the authoring agent as failures (blocked by #1151)

## Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart
```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS[JS runtime throw] -->|faAppError log record| ENG[JsAppEngine]
  HOST[Flutter render build throw] -->|reportHostError| ENG
  ENG -->|gate + publish| GATE[JsAppErrorChannel]
  GATE -->|onDeliver| SVC[AgentService]
  SVC -->|sendText: mid-run steer / idle fresh turn| TURN[system-notice turn]
  OPEN[open_app tool] --> PF{preflight gate}
  PF -->|test file + runner| FT[flutter-test gate]
  PF -->|else + engine bootable| SM[smoke render on scratch copy]
  FT -->|red| FAIL[failed tool result + excerpt]
  SM -->|no render / captured error| FAIL
  FT -->|green| LAUNCH[launcher opens the app]
  SM -->|clean first render| LAUNCH
```
</details>

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1246
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1246
- **Title**: gh-1164 [GOAL] built-in js-apps skill (promoted from app asset, decisive apps-vs-widget routing) + JS render/runtime errors reported back to the authoring agent as failures (blocked by #1151)
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1164` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 106
- **Additions**: +4102
- **Deletions**: -165
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T21:23:19Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T21:37:25Z

## PR Description

### What changed
`js-apps` is now a first-party core builtin (source of truth `prompts/skills/js-apps/SKILL.md`, embedded via `gen_prompts.dart`; the drift-able app asset and its seeder were retired, with per-platform stale-seed cleanup so old seeds stop shadowing the hardened skill). JS render/runtime/load errors now flow back to the authoring agent: the engine's bootstrap captures `jsr.showError`, timer/RAF callback throws, `onerror`/`unhandledrejection` and host render failures as structured `faAppError:` records, `JsAppErrorChannel` gates them (one report per app+fingerprint per source revision, per-app circuit breaker, bounded payloads) and delivers a system notice into the bound session (steered mid-run; a fresh turn while idle). The `open_app` tool gained a pre-flight gate that never reports success for an app that can't run: standing `test/apps/<id>_test.dart` via a `FlutterTestRunner` seam when the toolchain exists, otherwise an in-engine headless smoke render on a scratch copy (web-safe conditional-import probe); no gate is installed where no JS engine can boot.

### Key decisions
- Single skill file, no generated copy — drift guard now asserts the retired machinery stays gone; stale seeded copies are recognized by all six historical per-platform filter variants (the old seeder was platform-filtering).
- Engines only capture/forward; dedup, breaker, and delivery live in the channel so engines stay cheap and the smoke gate can pass a local collector.
- Dart-side engine-start failures are NOT republished as app errors (host-capability failures — E3: the channel is inert without a JS runtime).
- `testWidgets` skip is bool-only, so engine-dependent tests skip at the group level (existing suite convention).

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/skills test/apps test/prompts test/cli/skills_builtin_cli_test.dart
cd flutter_app && flutter test test/apps/ test/skills_toggles_store_test.dart test/agent_service_js_app_error_delivery_test.dart
```
Engine-dependent capture tests skip without the native JS bridge (issue #184), as the existing engine suite does. Full-suite failing sets match the pristine-HEAD environmental baseline (goldens/wasm/integration-CLI only).

<details><summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  JS[JS runtime throw] -->|faAppError log record| ENG[JsAppEngine]
  HOST[Flutter render build throw] -->|reportHostError| ENG
  ENG -->|gate + publish| GATE[JsAppErrorChannel]
  GATE -->|onDeliver| SVC[AgentService]
  SVC -->|sendText: mid-run steer / idle fresh turn| TURN[system-notice turn]
  OPEN[open_app tool] --> PF{preflight gate}
  PF -->|test file + runner| FT[flutter-test gate]
  PF -->|else + engine bootable| SM[smoke render on scratch copy]
  FT -->|red| FAIL[failed tool result + excerpt]
  SM -->|no render / captured error| FAIL
  FT -->|green| LAUNCH[launcher opens the app]
  SM -->|clean first render| LAUNCH
```
</details>
